subject: Biology
title: Peripheral & Autonomic Nervous Systems (ANS)
learningObjectives: Classify the 12 Cranial Nerves as Sensory, Motor, or Mixed
Describe the 31 pairs of Spinal Nerves and the monosynaptic stretch reflex arc
Contrast the Sympathetic (Thoracolumbar) and Parasympathetic (Craniosacral) divisions across target visceral organs
content:
### 10.1 Peripheral Nerve Organization

```
                        PERIPHERAL NERVE DISTRIBUTION
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                         ▼
  CRANIAL NERVES (12 Pairs in Amniotes)                   SPINAL NERVES (31 Pairs in Humans)
  ├── I to XII (Sensory, Motor, or Mixed)                 ├── All 31 pairs are MIXED NERVES
  └── Originates directly from Brain                      └── Attached to spinal cord via
                                                              ├── Dorsal Root (Sensory / DRG)
                                                              └── Ventral Root (Motor)
```

- **12 Cranial Nerve Pairs**:
  - **Sensory (3)**: CN I (Olfactory), CN II (Optic), CN VIII (Vestibulocochlear).
  - **Motor (5)**: CN III (Oculomotor), CN IV (Trochlear), CN VI (Abducens), CN XI (Accessory), CN XII (Hypoglossal).
  - **Mixed (4)**: CN V (Trigeminal), CN VII (Facial), CN IX (Glossopharyngeal), CN X (Vagus).
- **31 Spinal Nerve Pairs**: All 31 are **MIXED NERVES** (8 Cervical, 12 Thoracic, 5 Lumbar, 5 Sacral, 1 Coccygeal). Dorsal root carries afferent sensory fibers (DRG contains pseudounipolar cytons); Ventral root carries efferent motor fibers.

### 10.2 Autonomic Nervous System: Sympathetic vs. Parasympathetic

```
                          AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM (ANS)
                                        │
         ┌──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                             ▼
  SYMPATHETIC DIVISION ("Fight or Flight")                     PARASYMPATHETIC DIVISION ("Rest & Digest")
  ├── Thoracolumbar Outflow (T₁–L₂)                            ├── Craniosacral Outflow (CN III, VII, IX, X + S₂–S₄)
  ├── Short pre-ganglionic; Long post-ganglionic               ├── Long pre-ganglionic; Short post-ganglionic
  └── Post-ganglionic transmitter: Noradrenaline               └── Post-ganglionic transmitter: Acetylcholine
```

### 10.3 Visceral Target Organ Antagonism Matrix

| Visceral Target Organ | Sympathetic Effect ("Fight or Flight") | Parasympathetic Effect ("Rest & Digest") |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pupil of Eye (Iris)** | **Mydriasis** (Dilates pupil via radial muscle) | **Miosis** (Constricts pupil via circular muscle) |
| **Heart Rate & Force** | **Increases** heart rate & force of contraction | **Decreases** heart rate & force (via Vagus X) |
| **Bronchioles (Lungs)** | **Bronchodilation** (Expands airways for airflow) | **Bronchoconstriction** (Constricts airways) |
| **GI Tract & Motility** | **Inhibits** peristalsis & gastric secretions | **Stimulates** peristalsis & digestive secretions |
| **Salivary Glands** | Secretes small volume of thick, viscous saliva | Secretes large volume of watery, enzyme-rich saliva |
| **Urinary Bladder** | Relaxes Detrusor muscle; constricts sphincter | Contracts Detrusor muscle; relaxes sphincter (**Micturition**) |
| **Systemic Arterioles** | **Vasoconstriction** (Raises systemic BP) | No direct innervation (except erectile tissue) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Monosynaptic Knee-Jerk Reflex Arc
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Tapping the patellar tendon stretches quadriceps muscle spindles -> primary Ia afferent fires -> enters spinal cord via dorsal root -> monosynaptically excites alpha-motor neuron in ventral horn -> efferent action potential via ventral root contracts quadriceps -> leg kicks forward.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Sympathetic Adrenal Medulla Exception
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers directly innervate chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla (modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons) releasing 80% Epinephrine and 20% Norepinephrine directly into systemic blood.
